no62.summary: A secretary of Cardinal Pellevé, signing Baron, writes from Rome to Jean de Piles, abbé d'Orbais, the League's envoy, with the news of Henri III's death: couriers from Spain, Genoa and Tuscany, and the Duke of Lorraine's letter from his agent Bardin in Paris, 8 August ('le Roy a esté tué, et c'est le Roy de Navarre qui l'a faict faire'; the Cardinal de Bourbon proclaimed King in Paris). In cipher: '[Ƃ] depeschera [ʃ] dedans deux jours le doien', 'la protection que vous sçavez', Mons. Cassin (his senior, ill with fever), 'Mr le [τ] mon maistre', 'j'ay veu ung advis qui confirme', the signature Baron.
no62.en:
Sir, we never stop writing from here and have no news from you; I believe we shall have it often and safely from now
on. We had word here on the 17th of this month, by an extraordinary courier coming from Spain who had passed through
Lyon on the 12th, of the accident said to have befallen the King's person, on which no one relied; the letters of the
ordinary post of the 9th also mentioned it, and a courier from Genoa carrying letters of the 17th from there told many
particulars of it, and for all that no great credit was given to it until Sunday, when one arrived in the evening,
sent express by the Grand Duke of Tuscany to His Holiness, reporting that he had received one, also express, from the
Duke of Lorraine, with letters written at Nancy on the 11th of August;

snip.cap: BnF fr. 3413 f. 126v, to the abbé d’Orbais, 23 August 1589: Les jugemens de Dieu sont fort profons et inscrutables, then the cipher signs of depeschera, dedans deux jours
